problem: Obtain the representational benefit of predicting robot videos without requiring expensive video decoding before every control decision.
contribution: UVA jointly learns video/action latents with separate lightweight diffusion decoders. Policy inference can skip the video decoder. Input/output masking also supports forward dynamics, inverse dynamics and action-free video learning without presenting one capability's metric as another.
algorithm: Encode historical RGB through a pretrained VAE and historical high-rate action chunks through projections, concatenate with masked future visual tokens, and fuse with a transformer. Consistent token positions are masked across future frames. Independent video/action diffusion losses supervise lightweight heads; application-dependent masks select policy/dynamics/generation tasks. A policy-only ablation removes video supervision.
observations: Historical third-person RGB and action history; language CLIP conditioning for LIBERO. At policy time all future images are masked, so actual future observations are not available to the actor. The real-world UMI datasets use camera-related motion information; the inverse-dynamics evaluation is separately compared against motion-capture camera poses.
actions: Continuous action chunks, typically16predicted and8executed. Task-specific action meanings follow simulator/UMI control interfaces, not a universal joint-ID map. The paper's planning mode samples100DP-C trajectories, predicts their futures and executes the first6steps of the selected candidate.
embodiment_and_data: PushT,ToolHang,PushT-M,LIBERO10 and public UMI Cup/Towel/Mouse data evaluated with an ARX X5 arm. Multitask real training samples500episodes/task (1500total) from6764public episodes;20real rollouts/task. Supplemental video-pretraining experiment uses3175human videos, so large-scale actionless-video exploitation is still limited rather than absent.
experiments: Evaluate single/multitask policies, visual distribution shifts, history-length robustness, video FVD, block-pushing candidate selection and mocap-referenced inverse dynamics. Main LIBERO description uses50initializations/task and500total; appendixX-B contains an inconsistent10runs wording, while TableVIII explicitly confirms50/task in the500test setting. Best-checkpoint selection must not be confused with an untouched final evaluation.
baselines: CNN/transformer Diffusion Policy, improved CLIP/ViT DP-UMI, OpenVLA,pi0/pi0FAST and a third-party UniPi implementation. Inputs/pretraining differ:pi0 uses additional wrist/proprioception and broader data. Timing matches8executed actions by querying OpenVLA8times, not comparing a single forward call directly.

quantitative_result.physical_success: Multitask Cup13/20,Towel14/20,Mouse16/20 versus DP-UMI10/20,14/20,8/20; single-task Cup17/20 versus19/20 baseline.
quantitative_result.runtime: 95ms per16-action chunk at16denoising steps on RTX3080, versus70ms DP-UMI. Breakdown40msVAE+40mstransformer+15msaction head; NOT measured on NX.
quantitative_result.other_metric: PDFp10 TableVI inverse camera-pose error0.75cm/1.11deg versus SLAM0.41cm/0.30deg; this is not physical task success.

limitations: Some visual changes still cause large failures (PushT background-color success0.35 versus0.98normal). Single-task cup performance is worse than DP-UMI, and longer history can underuse failure-recovery data. UMI camera-pose reconstruction accuracy does not guarantee general inverse dynamics. The block-pushing text's50% unconditioned-policy ceiling is distinct from the planner's60% and simulator-selected75%; video FVD is likewise separate from control success.
code_and_license: Primary paper links https://unified-video-action-model.github.io/ and says implementation derives from pretrained MAR-B with substantial modifications. Repository, encoder/checkpoint and UMI/human-video license texts were not inspected; all those reuse terms are NOT_AUDITED. No code executed.
hardware_adaptation: COMPARE a compact auxiliary future-image objective or decoupled action head against the actual ACT baseline. The0.5B backbone and VAE require measured NX memory/latency; RTX3080 timing cannot establish Wi-Fi or Orin deadlines. Preserve commanded-action history, chunk timing and source camera calibration. Pi remains a capture/servo node and should not be required to decode video predictions for every command.
